parts.text: Chops stands by the west wood and sells the logs to carpenters.
Mines until the pack is heavy, then walks the ore to the bank.
Fishes the south docks and talks about the weather more than the catch.
Fills bulk orders for the smiths and counts the reward points aloud.
Hawks wood and hides on the bank steps and keeps coin in the box.
Copies runes for a house library when the day's work is done.
Walks with miners on the mountain road and watches the trees for reds.
Tends a vendor stall in a Britain house and pays the upkeep from sales.
Reads house signs for greatly worn boards and tells the tavern.
Digs sand for the glassblower and hates a wet boot.
Takes hides to the tanner and sells the rest at the provisioner.
Smelts ore at the forge and argues about ingot prices.
Banks the catch as a check so the pack stays light.
Favours the Yew road for tall trees and fewer crowds.
Buys tools in Trinsic because the steel holds.
Takes the public moongate home when the pack is full.
Sits the carpenter's fire after selling and listens to town talk.
Sharpens the pick at dusk and lays out the next hill.
Walks the docks to look at small boats still out of reach.
Runs Britain from bank to smith to docks and knows the short ways.
Hauls sand at dawn and talks to no one until the bank is done.
Smokes hides behind the tanner and judges the wind like a cook.
Walks the boardwalk of Britain and prices every crate by eye.
Pushes a cart of ore toward Minoc and counts the hills aloud.
Mends nets in Skara and sells the extra catch at the island stall.
Fills Trinsic bulk orders and keeps a tally on a scrap of hide.
Saws fallen oak on the Yew road and stacks it by the shrine path.
Marks Vesper crates and argues with the clerk about wet wood.
Times the public gate so the pack hits the banker before the crowd.
Keeps a ledger in the tavern and pretends it is only ale talk.
Banks after dark so the line is short and the thieves are obvious.
Walks the Britain graveyard at dusk and counts bones, not hours.
Takes the Despise road one troll at a time and will not enter the caves.
Runs champion altars for scrolls and skulls and counts the waves out loud.
Stands anti-PK on the mountain road and escorts ore when asked.
Drills with Order steel and talks virtue only when the blade is clean.
Rides with Chaos when the horns sound and sleeps in borrowed halls.
Practises the bow behind Trinsic until the quiver is empty.
Keeps a spellbook dry and reagents counted before any talk.
Guards a public rune library and charges a coin for a mark.
Prefers Felucca altars because the rewards are meaner and better.
Sells body-escorts through red land and names the price up front.
Walks the Virtue shrines between hunts and keeps the titles honest.
Leads a small crew and will not start until every shield is on.
Hunts the gate road and leaves the dungeon mouth to braver fools.
Tithes at the shrine before steel, even on a thin day.
Works the Jhelom pits with a lute and a blade, in that order.
Digs treasure when the map is good and the crew can hold a spawn.
Hunts Trammel when the bones need practice and Felucca when they need gold.
Farms champion scrolls to sell and talks of little else.
Calls guards first and steel second, unless the name is already red.
Sweeps the Britain yard at first light and leaves before the tourists.
Runs Wrong when the crew is sharp and Shame when they are not.
Prefers Ice over Fire and will tell you why until you walk away.
Drills on Trinsic's sand and counts the missed parries out loud.
Bets on the Jhelom pits and then fights the winner for practice.
Buys reagents in Moonglow and hides the good ones in a book.
Watches the Felucca gate for reds and sells the warning cheap.
Sells champion scrolls at the bank and will not haggle twice.
Names a body-escort fee before the first step into red land.
Oils the blade at a shrine and calls it prayer if anyone asks.
Takes the night watch on a guild road and sleeps after the second bell.
Works the crowded bank and watches open packs more than faces.
Lifts from the bank steps and is gone before the shout.
Prefers Britain's night crowd, when the guards are tired.
Cuts purses in Jhelom and sells the rest through a quiet fence.
Hunts stealable museum pieces and knows which houses leave a window.
Leaves trapped chests where greed walks first.
Has seen fake gold piles work and will not touch one.
Reads vendor prices twice and still assumes a cheat.
Will not follow a stranger's gate after a withdraw.
Stands in shadow by the banker and counts footsteps.
Practises lockpicking on empty houses and leaves the good doors.
Sells through Buccaneer's Den and does not ask names.
Works Nujel'm's heat and crowded halls, where hands wander.
Keeps empty hands in the open and a full pack under the cloak.
Will not fight a pack. One guard is already too many.
Lifts dyed cloth when the owner looks at the banker.
Prefers checks to coin piles. Less noise when they vanish.
Leaves by moongate, never by the same road twice.
Watches gray names at the bank and lets the loud ones feed first.
Knows which Britain roofs look into shop courtyards.
Works Vesper's warehouse crowds when the clerks shout over crates.
Waits where miners pay out and never stands in the same shadow twice.
Watches Trinsic's gates for fat packs and thin guards.
Lifts on the Skara ferry, where everyone looks at the water.
Walks the Luna mall as if shopping and leaves with quieter goods.
Prefers Umbra's night, where a cloak is just another shadow.
Knows which banker hour makes the line long and the eyes tired.
Studies pack straps the way a smith studies a weld.
Practises leaving before a shout can finish a name.
Folds checks small and never counts them in a street.
Leaves at dawn, never at the same bell twice.
Walks the fields west of Britain with a dog that stays.
Hangs about horse sellers and judges the gait before the price.
Prefers ostards and the open ground they were born for.
Leads a pack llama on gathering runs and lets the beast carry the ore.
Donates extra creatures to the public zoo and keeps the rare hues.
Sits the bonding hours like a watch and talks to the animal, not the town.
Learned enough veterinary work to keep a follower standing.
Will not take a young beast into a dungeon. The field is enough.
Started on sheep and still respects a calm flock.
Works the Yew woods for a wolf that will heel.
Pays stable rent without complaint. A lost follower is worse than gold.
Looks at dragons the way a child looks at a castle. Later. Not now.
Talks pet hues in the tavern and forgets to finish the ale.
Escorts gatherers with a bear on a short command.
Gates with a mount and hates a town that forbids it.
Learned from Skara rangers to keep the beast between you and the road.
Keeps meat in a pouch and never lets the follower starve on a long walk.
Names every follower and will not sell one that has a name.
Watches tamers show off in Britain and leaves before the crowd thickens.
Dreams of a nightmare and trains on horses until the dream is earned.
Walks Cove's shore with a dog that hates boats and loves crabs.
Helps Skara herders move sheep and learns patience the hard way.
Looks for a hind in Yew and will not take one that will not stay.
Pays Britain's stable and checks the stall before the tavern.
Walks Moonglow's zoo path and notes which cages still have room.
Runs ostards on open sand and hates a town cobble under their feet.
Works a bear on a short command and never in a crowded street.
Starts bonding at dawn so the hours end before the drunks arrive.
Buys meat at first bell and will not feed a follower cheap scraps.
Keeps a book of follower names and will not reuse one.
Walks the field at dusk when the town has gone indoors.
Mines the hills north of Minoc from first light and never takes the same tunnel twice.
Swings a pick in the Covetous mine and keeps one eye on the tunnel mouth.
Walks the Vesper mine every morning and sings to keep the headache away.
Digs the cliffs behind Cove and carries the ore to Britain on foot.
Taps each rock twice before mining it, for luck and for nothing else.
Counts the swings of the pick and rests at every hundredth one.
Keeps two spare shovels in the bank and one more in the pack.
Smelts every load at the Minoc forge because the fire there burns hotter.
Hammers out daggers at the anvil until the blacksmith skill ticks up.
Makes cutlasses for the Jhelom duelists and sells them by the dozen.
Repairs armour for fighters outside the smithy for a small fee.
Hangs about the Britain forge and offers to fix any dented shield.
Carries a smith hammer in the belt even when there is no work to do.
Sorts ingots by colour of the ore and stacks them in neat rows.
Walks the mountain road to Minoc with a mule and a sour look.
Mines until the guards change shift and then goes to eat.
Eats a leg of mutton at the mine mouth before every dig.
Works the Shame entrance cave and flees when the elementals wake.
Mines on Delucia's mountains, where few reds bother to look.
Digs the Papua hills after the rain, when the rock splits easy.
Keeps a list of good mining spots and shares it with no one.
Makes plate helms at night and sells them at the Trinsic smithy at dawn.
Stands at the anvil so long the neighbours know the hammer by its ring.
Tests each new sword on a practice dummy before selling it.
Melts down old armour from the dungeon crews and makes it new again.
Buys cheap tongs in bulk and resells them to new smiths.
Takes the ore to the forge in small loads so no thief gets a full pack.
Shouts the price of iron from the Britain bank steps at noon.
Swaps ingots for fish with the dock folk and calls it a fair trade.
Mines alone and whistles so the bears know someone is there.
Stops mining when the pick handle cracks and walks home to buy another.
Hammers shields for the Order guild and asks for their colours in return.
Wears the same leather apron every day and patches it with hide scraps.
Sits on the mountain ledge above Minoc and watches the smoke of the forges.
Cleans the anvil with a rag after every job, even the small ones.
Mines in the Yew hills where the rock is soft and the trees hide the road.
Wakes before dawn to beat the other miners to the best cave.
Gives broken picks to new miners so they can learn the swing.
Keeps a small fire going in the mine to scare off the ratmen.
Carries the ingots to the Vesper bank across the bridge, never around it.
Hauls ore from the Minoc cave with a pack horse that knows the way.
Forges bardiches and halberds for the guards and gets paid in coin.
Trades nails and hinges to the carpenters on the Britain waterfront.
Mines slowly and talks about the old days when ore was cheap.
Hides the good ore spots from the young miners with a wink.
Stands at the forge in Jhelom and listens to the duel pit crowd.
Makes ringmail for new fighters at a price they can pay.
Hammers a horseshoe every morning though no one buys horseshoes.
Keeps a lump of ore on the windowsill as a souvenir of the first dig.
Buys iron from new miners at the bank and smelts it at a profit.
Studies the anvil sparks as if they tell the weather.
Sharpens swords for anyone who stops and pays a few coins.
Finishes each day by counting ingots out loud in the bank.
Mines in the rain because the other miners stay indoors.
Fixes the pick with rope when there is no coin for a new one.
Smiths a chain coif for every friend who joins a hunting crew.
Mines the cave near the Britain graveyard and ignores the moaning.
Leaves one ingot at the shrine every week and says nothing about it.
Walks the Minoc bridge twice before starting work, to wake the legs.
Carries salt and bread in the pack for the long mining days.
Bangs the pick on the rock to call a friend in the next tunnel.
Mines until the pack groans and then mines one more swing.
Sells kryss and war forks to the fencers in Serpent's Hold.
Runs the bellows for the old smith in Vesper and learns by watching.
Stamps a small mark on every blade so buyers know the maker.
Talks to the rock while mining and swears it answers.
Tries every mountain on the map once before choosing a favourite.
Mines by lantern light in the deep caves and hums to fill the quiet.
Brings a spare lantern because the first one always goes out.
Keeps the forge fire low at night and wakes up to stir it.
Makes war axes for the Minoc miners, who like a tool that bites.
Carries a small whetstone and uses it while waiting in line.
Trades a sword for a meal at the Minoc inn when coin is short.
Smiths only exceptional pieces and melts the rest without a word.
Puts the hammer down at noon to eat and watch the carts go by.
Tells every new smith to practise on daggers until the arm aches.
Mines near the Wrong dungeon hills and runs at the first odd noise.
Buys a new pickaxe at the tinker every week and wears it out by Sunday.
Works the Trinsic forge in the heat and drinks water by the bucket.
Wraps the hands in cloth before a long day at the anvil.
Hauls ingots to the house and stacks them by the front door.
Keeps a sword on the wall that was the first one ever made.
Mines the island hills off Moonglow and rows back before dark.
Stands by the forge and tells stories of cave-ins to scare apprentices.
Makes studded leather cuffs on the side for extra coin.
Smelts ore with a friend and splits the ingots down the middle.
Walks to the Minoc tavern after every dig and orders the same stew.
Checks the pick for cracks before and after every tunnel.
Rests in the shade of the mine mouth when the sun is high.
Mines on the hill east of Britain and sells ore to the city smiths.
Asks every passing fighter what weapon they need next week.
Fills the forge with coal at dusk and leaves it to glow.
Sends a friend the first ingot of every new vein as a gift.
Mines with a torch in the belt and a candle in the pack.
Pounds out scale armour pieces until the fingers go numb.
Grumbles about the price of iron and still buys a full load.
Takes a nap in the mine mouth after the midday meal.
Leaves the anvil clean and the tongs hung before going home.
Hammers the dents out of helms for the Britain guards at cost.
Mines only in the morning and smiths only in the afternoon.
Keeps a book of weapon orders and crosses them off one by one.
Brings ingots to the Serpent's Hold smith and argues over quality.
Watches for ettins on the mountain road and hides behind rocks.
Walks the ore past the Britain bank so the crowd sees a hard worker.
Sells old picks at half price to beggars who want to start mining.
Knocks the dust off the boots at the smithy door every time.
Checks the ore for flecks of colour and grins at every speck.
Repairs broken weapons after the Despise crews come home.
Buys ale for the miners who share good tunnels.
Swings the pick in rhythm with an old Minoc work song.
Digs in the caves of Buccaneer's Den and keeps a dagger close.
Visits the Moonglow smith to trade tips on tempering blades.
Carries ore in two small bags so the weight sits even.
Chops oak in the Yew forest until the axe blade needs a rest.
Fells trees near the Britain farms and piles the logs by the fence.
Cuts wood in the Moonglow woods and ferries it to the mainland.
Splits kindling every morning for the bakers and takes bread in trade.
Carries an axe on the shoulder and whistles through the trees.
Chops until the pack is heavy and then drags the logs to the carpenter.
Marks good trees with a notch and comes back the next day.
Chops wood in the Trinsic forest and watches for wild boars.
Builds chairs and stools at the carpenter's bench in Britain.
Makes wooden chests for anyone who brings the logs.
Carves small wooden boxes as gifts for new neighbours.
Builds bookcases for the scribes of Moonglow and asks for books in return.
Sands every table twice before calling it done.
Keeps a pile of sawdust in the corner and burns it in the winter.
Makes bows at the Yew bowyer and tests each one on the range.
Fletches arrows at night by candle and bundles them by the hundred.
Plucks chickens on the farm for feathers to fletch arrows.
Sells arrows at the Britain bank to the archers leaving for Shame.
Carves crossbow stocks and lets the tinker fit the triggers.
Tests the string of every bow three times before selling it.
Buys feathers from the farmers in Britain and pays in logs.
Chops at dawn when the woods are wet and the axe bites deep.
Hauls logs to the Vesper shipwright and watches the boats being built.
Builds a new stool every day and gives the old one away.
Cuts yew for the bowyers and asks the woods for pardon first.
Rests under the biggest tree in Yew after every load.
Chops trees along the road to Skara ferry and sells to travellers.
Carves walking sticks and quarterstaffs from fallen branches.
Makes gnarled staves for the mages of Moonglow on order.
Spends the evening fixing broken chairs in the tavern.
Measures every log with a string and writes the length on it.
Keeps the axe sharp with a stone and oil every noon.
Chops alone deep in the woods and talks to the squirrels.
Builds shelves for the new house owners and charges by the shelf.
Watches for reapers in the deep Yew woods and never chops near one.
Stacks logs in the house until the door will barely open.
Makes wooden shields for the militia and paints them blue.
Carves toy soldiers from scraps and gives them to town children.
Cuts wood near the Yew abbey and listens to the monks at prayer.
Fletches arrows on the bank steps and sells them still warm.
Builds armoires that take three days and sell in an hour.
Chops wood in the snow near the northern pass and curses the cold.
Keeps a list of which carpenters pay the best for logs.
Carves a small wooden horse for every tamer who asks.
Builds tables for the Britain inns and eats at each one once.
Buys shafts from new bowyers and finishes them into arrows.
Makes long bows for the rangers of Skara and trades for venison.
Chops until the arms ache and then rests by a stream.
Sings a woodcutter's song to keep a steady swing.
Fixes the Britain docks with fresh wood when the planks rot.
Collects fallen branches for kindling on the walk home.
Checks the woods for giant spiders before starting to chop.
Makes looms and spinning wheels for the tailors of Britain.
Carves wooden bowls and spoons and sells them to the cooks.
Chops wood in the Cove woods and carries it through the orc camps.
Builds barrels for the Vesper brewers and tastes the first batch.
Makes fishing poles from thin branches and gives them to beggars.
Splits logs with a war axe because it was cheaper than a hatchet.
Chops trees near the Minoc road and trades wood for ore.
Carves the name of the owner into every chest made to order.
Builds benches for the Britain park and sits on each one.
Tests each arrow shaft by rolling it on the table.
Fletches crossbow bolts for the Serpent's Hold guards.
Hauls a cart of logs to Trinsic every tenth day.
Carves a mark on the tree stump after each fell.
Sells firewood to the inns when winter comes early.
Makes heavy crossbows only for friends who promise to use them well.
Builds furniture with no nails, only wooden pegs, out of pride.
Watches the wood grain for flaws before starting a new chair.
Keeps sawdust in the pockets and leaves a trail through town.
Chops at the edge of the woods so the town is always in sight.
Visits the Yew bowyer every week to trade stories and shafts.
Builds a training dummy for every new fighter who asks nicely.
Carves little birds from pine and hangs them in the window.
Takes the ferry to Moonglow with logs and comes back with reagents.
Makes composite bows at the bench and argues about the best wood.
Burns the bark in the evening fire because it smells of the woods.
Chops trees by the Britain river and floats the logs downstream.
Builds boxes for the fishermen to store their catch.
Carves runes into wooden plaques for the rune library shelves.
Fixes wagon wheels for the farmers outside Britain.
Oils every new table with lamp oil until it shines.
Makes wooden clubs for the young fighters of Jhelom.
Cuts cedar near Nujel'm and sells the scent as much as the wood.
Builds a small shrine of wood near the Yew road and keeps it clean.
Chops wood with a friend and races to fill the pack first.
Measures twice and cuts once, and tells everyone about it.
Collects bird nests from felled trees and brings them to the tamers.
Builds wooden stairs for the house owners on the hills.
Fletches arrows with grey goose feathers and swears they fly truer.
Sells bows at the Trinsic range to the archers practising there.
Rebuilds the fences of the Britain farms after every storm.
Makes wooden crates for the Vesper warehouses in bulk.
Carves pipes from briar root and smokes one after work.
Builds a bench outside the house for passing travellers to rest.
Makes practice bows for children and teaches them to aim.
Chops oak and ash but will never cut a very old tree.
Carries a small saw in the belt for quick repairs in town.
Stacks the logs in a pyramid and counts them from the top.
Builds bedframes for the Britain inns and tests each one with a nap.
Keeps a wooden spoon in the pack to stir any stew at any camp.
Fells trees near Trinsic's walls and watches the guards train.
Carves a new axe handle each season from a straight branch.
Makes arrows in the tavern and gives the bent ones to the fire.
Walks to the Yew bowyer in the rain and dries the bows by the hearth.
Chops trees on the islands and ferries logs across the bay.
Shears sheep on the farms west of Britain and spins the wool at home.
Spins yarn at the wheel in the tailor shop and hums a tavern tune.
Weaves bolts of cloth on the loom and stacks them by colour.
Sews fancy shirts for the nobles of Britain and charges double.
Makes floppy hats for the farmers and gives the first one free.
Dyes cloth in the back of the tailor shop and stains both hands.
Picks cotton in the Britain fields at dawn before the heat.
Pulls flax near Vesper and sells the bundles to the weavers.
Cuts leather armour for the archers of Yew from deer hides.
Buys hides from hunters at the bank and turns them into tunics.
Sews robes for the mages of Moonglow and embroiders the hems.
Makes bandages from spare cloth and gives them to the healers.
Keeps a pincushion on the wrist and forgets it is there.
Dyes a new shirt every day and never wears the same colour twice.
Sews sandals for the Nujel'm crowd and hears all the gossip.
Makes cloaks for the travellers leaving the Britain gate.
Takes measurements with a knotted string and a sharp eye.
Stitches torn clothes for the Jhelom duelists for a coin each.
Buys cheap dyes from the Britain tailor and mixes new shades.
Tans hides by the river and keeps the smell away from town.
Makes studded armour on order for the Serpent's Hold guards.
Sews bags and pouches from leather scraps and sells them cheap.
Makes a new apron for every smith who comes to the shop.
Spins wool on the Skara ferry to pass the crossing.
Weaves carpets on a big loom in the house and sells them slowly.
Sews a hidden pocket into every cloak made for friends.
Knits a scarf in the winter for every miner on the Minoc road.
Bakes bread at the Britain bakery before the sun is up.
Grinds wheat at the mill and carries the flour to the bakers.
Cooks fish steaks on the docks for the tired fishermen.
Roasts ribs over a campfire outside town and sells them hot.
Bakes cakes on feast days and gives slices to the guards.
Makes pies with apples from the Britain orchard in the autumn.
Cooks stew in a big pot at the tavern and never gives out the recipe.
Bakes cookies for the children of Trinsic every week.
Buys eggs from the farm and fries them for travellers at dawn.
Makes sausage from pork and hangs it in the smokehouse.
Picks carrots and lettuce at the farm and sells them at the market.
Cooks bird meat on a stick at the Yew crossroads.
Bakes muffins and sells them outside the Britain bank.
Makes cheese from the farm milk and ages it in the cellar.
Cooks for the guild hall and asks for no pay but the leftovers.
Brews ale in a barrel in the back room and tastes it every day.
Makes wine from the Magincia grapes and gives it a proud name.
Picks berries in the Yew woods and bakes them into tarts.
Fries bacon on the Vesper docks and the smell pulls a crowd.
Sells cooked chicken legs to hungry fighters at the Britain gate.
Makes pizza with cheese and sausage for the tavern on busy nights.
Cooks for the miners in Minoc and keeps a pot on the fire all day.
Fishes the river under the Britain bridge until the sun goes down.
Casts a line off the Vesper pier and talks to every passer.
Fishes from a small boat in the bay near Magincia.
Sails out to deep water to fish for big catches and sea serpents.
Fishes the lake near Yew and eats the catch by the water.
Cleans fish on the docks with a sharp knife and quick hands.
Sells fresh trout at the market every morning.
Fishes in the rain and swears the fish bite better when wet.
Keeps a lucky fishing pole that was a gift from a grandfather.
Fishes off the Trinsic docks and watches the ships come in.
Cooks the catch on a campfire right on the beach.
Fishes near Jhelom and sells to the fighters at the pits.
Throws back the small fish and talks to them before they go.
Fishes the Serpent's Hold harbour with a heavy line.
Checks the boat for leaks every morning before rowing out.
Fishes at night by lantern on the Moonglow docks.
Rows out past the Britain breakwater to find quiet water.
Fishes with a friend and bets on who lands the biggest.
Dries fish on a rack behind the house for the winter.
Sails to Buccaneer's Den to sell fish no honest dock will buy.
Fishes the Ocllo shore and knows every rock by name.
Mends the boat sail by candle when the wind tears it.
Keeps a tally of every big fish on the wall of the house.
Fishes until the bait runs out and then goes to the tavern.
Walks the beach at low tide looking for shells and lost coins.
Fishes the cold water near the Ice isle and wears three cloaks.
Sails to Nujel'm with a hold of fish and sells to the palace cooks.
Waits on the dock for the fishing boats and buys the catch cheap.
Carves fish hooks from bone and trades them at the docks.
Cooks fish soup for the dock workers every noon.
Fishes off the Skara Brae docks and listens to the bards across the water.
Shears sheep in spring and sells the wool all year.
Sews dresses for the brides of Britain and cries at every wedding.
Makes jester suits for the bards and laughs at each fitting.
Tailors leather gloves for the smiths and asks for a sword in trade.
Sells tunics at the Vesper market and folds them neat on the table.
Dyes robes black for the mages and red for the fighters.
Bakes bread with a friend and argues over the salt.
Cooks lamb chops for the nobles of Serpent's Hold on feast nights.
Grills fish at the Trinsic docks and sings to the gulls.
Weaves baskets from reeds by the river and sells them to farmers.
Tans leather in the Britain tannery and keeps the vats stirred.
Stitches the guild symbol on every tabard for a fair price.
Knits socks by the tavern fire and gives them to the poor.
Salts fish in barrels and ships them to Minoc for the miners.
Roasts a whole pig on a spit for the guild feast each month.
Kneads dough before the bakery opens and whistles while working.
Picks onions in the fields and weeps a little every time.
Makes honey cakes from market honey and sells out by noon.
Gathers herbs in the Yew woods for the kitchen and the healer.
Cooks a meal for every stranger who helps with the harvest.
Bakes bread in a clay oven behind the house in Skara Brae.
Fishes from the rocks near Cove and keeps an eye out for orcs.
Sells cut cloth to new tailors so they can learn the trade.
Cooks travel rations for the dungeon crews and packs them in cloth.
Sews a patch on every cloak that comes back from Despise torn.
Keeps a bowl of dough rising by the window on warm mornings.
Trades cooked meals for hides and turns the hides into boots.
Shops at every tailor in Britain to compare the dye colours.
Fishes near the Papua shore and eats the fish with jungle fruit.
Dries herbs from the Delucia fields on strings in the kitchen.
Writes scrolls in the Moonglow library and never spills a drop of ink.
Copies spells into books for new mages and charges by the circle.
Buys blank scrolls in bulk and fills them with recall spells to sell.
Makes runebooks for the travellers of Britain and names each one.
Sells scrolls of greater heal to the healers before a big hunt.
Reads every book in the Britain library once a year.
Writes a small book of town news and leaves it at the tavern.
Scribes spells by candle late at night and sleeps in the chair.
Trades scrolls for reagents at the Moonglow mage shop.
Mixes heal potions at the alchemist's table in Britain.
Grinds reagents with a mortar and pestle until the arm hurts.
Buys empty bottles from the tavern and fills them with potions.
Sells explosion potions to the dungeon crews heading for Deceit.
Brews cure potions and gives them to anyone bitten by spiders.
Picks garlic and ginseng in the fields for the potion table.
Keeps a row of potions on the shelf, sorted by colour.
Tests each potion with a sip and makes an awful face.
Mixes refresh potions for the miners who work long days.
Makes nightsight potions for the cave workers at a small price.
Brews poison potions and sells them only to people who ask twice.
Builds tools at the tinker's bench and sells them to new crafters.
Makes lockpicks and keeps quiet about who buys them.
Builds clocks and gives them to the houses that need time.
Tinkers sextants for the ship captains of Vesper.
Makes scissors and needles for the tailors in bulk.
Builds small traps to keep the rats out of the storehouse.
Makes jewellery from gold and gems and sells rings to lovers.
Fixes broken tools for free on the first day of each week.
Makes spyglasses and watches the ships from the tower.
Builds a new kind of lamp every month and none of them work.
